title: Weil restriction of algebraic spaces along finite locally free scheme maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:Z\to T$ be a finite locally free morphism of $S$-schemes [def-pc-finite-locally-free], with rank allowed to vary and to be zero. Let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with a morphism $E\to Z$. On $S$-schemes over $T$, define $R(T'\to T)=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(Z\times_TT',E)$, with restriction given by precomposition with base change and fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There is an algebraic space $R$ over $T$ whose functor of points is naturally isomorphic to this functor; this space is the Weil restriction $\operatorname{Res}_{Z/T}(E)$. No separation, quasi-compactness, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $E\to Z$ is required.

source.place: Tag 05YF (proposition-restriction-of-scalars-algebraic-space), criteria.tex, specialized to scheme Z and T.

proof.text: Write $q:E\to Z$ for the given map and give $E$ the $T$-structure $p\circ q$. Regard $T$ and $Z$ as their representable algebraic spaces using [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-relative-hom-space] with targets $X=E$ and $X=Z$, both times using precisely the given finite locally free map $p:Z\to T$. Obtain algebraic spaces $A=H_{Z,E/T}$ and $B=H_{Z,Z/T}$ over $T$, with the natural point descriptions in that node. This does not require any property of $q$.

source.place: Tag 05YF (proposition-restriction-of-scalars-algebraic-space), first sentence, applying Tag 05Y7 twice.

proof.text: The rule $(a,b)\mapsto(a,q\circ b)$ defines $c:A\to B$. The rule $a:U\to T\mapsto(a,\operatorname{pr}_Z:U\times_TZ\to Z)$ defines $e:h_T\to B$. Both commute with restriction because composition with $q$ and the projection commute with base change. They are therefore morphisms of algebraic spaces, since [def-trf-algebraic-space] defines these as natural transformations. Their maps to $T$ both retain $a$, so both are over $T$.

source.place: Tag 05YE (lemma-fibre-diagram), explicit maps of the displayed cartesian diagram.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the sheaf fibre product $P=A\times_{c,B,e}h_T$ is an algebraic space, over $T$ through its second projection. On a scheme $U$, a point is a pair $((a,b),a')$ satisfying $(a,q\circ b)=(a',\operatorname{pr}_Z)$. Equivalently $a=a'$ and $q\circ b=\operatorname{pr}_Z$. For a fixed $a:U\to T$, this says exactly that $b:U\times_TZ\to E$ is a $Z$-morphism. Conversely any such $b$ is automatically a $T$-morphism because $p\circ q\circ b=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_Z=a\circ\operatorname{pr}_U$. The inverse maps send $((a,b),a)$ to $b$ and $b$ to $((a,b),a)$; precomposition with $V\times_TZ\to U\times_TZ$ commutes with both. Thus $P$ has naturally the required functor of points, with the specified restriction maps. The argument uses neither positive constant rank nor an extra hypothesis on $q$.
